newsitem.title: USA: Congress clears five-year balanced budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Congress clears five-year balanced budget deal.

text.p: Congress Thursday gave final approval to a historic budget agreement which aims to bring the federal deficit to zero by 2002 and cut taxes by a net $85 billion over five years.
The Senate approved the final version of the budget on a bipartisan vote of 76 to 22 shortly after the House approved it 327 to 97.

Before the vote, the two chairmen of the House and Senate tax writing committees pledged in a joint letter to uphold the spirit of the agreement and hold the net cost of the tax cut to no more than $250 billion over ten years. Some had feared the tax cut could balloon by 2007 and put the government back into a deficit.

The budget agreement does not go to President Clinton for his signature but was worked out with the administration. It serves as a blueprint for spending and tax legislation which will be crafted this summer and those bills will need his approval to become law.

Wednesday, a key panel took the first concrete action to translate the budget into law. The House Ways and Means health subcommittee unanimously approved a broad plan to restructure the Medicare programme and cut spending by $115 billion over five years.
The House Ways and Means Committee is expected to start work next week on the total $135 billion five-year tax cut. All tax bills must originate in the House.
